description.narrative: The Project will support BCP, Perus largest bank, in expanding access to finance for sustainable construction and climate-smart agriculture. Sustainable buildings reduce environmental impacts by conserving energy and water, using sustainable materials, and reducing waste, while improving occupant health and well-being. Peru is also a major agricultural exporter, with the sector accounting for 6% of GDP and 16% of total exports. Agriculture is highly vulnerable to climate change and natural disastersfloods, droughts, earthquakes, and landslideswhich are frequent in Peru, and it contributes 13% of the countrys GHG emissions. Providing tailored finance for green construction and climate-smart agricultural practices through the Project will help address Perus climate vulnerabilities and mitigate emissions in these sectors. The Project will also support BCPs SME and WSME lending. The MSME finance gap in Peru is estimated at 4.7%; however, this low gap for formal enterprises masks the fact that only 27.8% of MSMEs access the regulated financial system. Informal demandestimated at US$14 billionexceeds the formal gap of US$10 billion. Women entrepreneurs generally have lower incomes, more limited access to finance than men, and smaller, more informal businesses. IFC will track: (i) the number and volume of outstanding climate finance loans; (ii) the share of climate finance in BCPs total portfolio; (iii) the number and volume of outstanding SME loans and their share of the portfolio; and (iv) the number and volume of outstanding WSME loans and their share within SME lending. At the market level, the Project is expected to support sustainability in the Peruvian financial sector by helping BCP position itself as a leader in green construction financing and by increasing market awareness and capacity related to EDGE certification, sending a strong signal that may encourage other financial institutions to expand sustainable construction lending.

The proposed investment (the Project) involves an up to 10 -year subordinated loan financing package of up to US$400 million (out of which up to US$250 million for IFCs own account and up to US$150 million for the account of B or parallel lenders) to Banco de Credito del Peru (BCP or the Bank), the largest commercial bank in Peru. The loan proceeds will be used to finance (i) green buildings (GB), (ii) climate smart agriculture (CSA), and (iii) small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and women-owned SMEs (WSMEs).
